C1_nested_restriction.note: Restriction maps compose; nested and overlapping restrictions of ONE global state agree automatically. This is the necessary direction and it is a theorem (partial trace is a conditional expectation).

C2_bell_chain.analytic_proof: If rho_AB is pure then any extension satisfies rho_ABC = rho_AB (x) rho_C (purity => no correlations with C), so rho_BC = Tr_A(rho_AB) (x) rho_C = (I/2) (x) rho_C, whose fidelity with Phi+ is 1/2 != 1. Overlap agreement is necessary, not sufficient (entanglement monogamy).

C3_quantitative_obstruction.note: Linear objective over the convex set of 3-qubit states (SDP). The optimum is strictly below 2: the two requested Bell marginals cannot coexist; the gap is the quantitative size of the obstruction.

C4_werner_thresholds.note: W(p) = p Phi+ + (1-p) I/4 on each listed pair, with identical overlaps by construction. The largest p admitting a common global state is computed by SDP; above it the pairwise-consistent family has no global realization.

C5_classical_contrast.chain_note: Classically, two marginals sharing one variable ALWAYS have a joint (Markov gluing). The quantum Bell chain fails. The obstruction in C2 is specifically quantum (monogamy), not a bookkeeping failure.
C5_classical_contrast.cycle_note: Even classically, overlap agreement on a CYCLE is not sufficient (three pairwise perfectly anticorrelated bits). Sufficiency of overlap agreement is a property of acyclic (tree) access structures in the classical case and fails already for a chain in the quantum case.

C6_inconsistent_overlap.note: Disagreeing overlaps are infeasible at once: overlap agreement is the necessary condition every sector's effective environment must satisfy.
